decisions.question: Rewrite the pasted delivery prompt with the review’s fixes and queue it after TC6?

options.label: Rewrite and queue

options.summary: No changes beyond TC6.

decisions.question: Point 7, a smoke test of the packaged program: MUST or SHOULD?

options.label: MUST, STACKSPEC 8.0.0
options.summary: Every product that ships a packaged program has CI start it and exercise every worker; a major version.

options.label: SHOULD, STACKSPEC 7.2.0
options.summary: Recommended but not required; stays minor.

decisions.question: Point 8: where is the delivery log kept?

options.label: Release notes
options.summary: Appended to the GitHub release of each train: durable, no commits to main.

options.label: delivery-log branch
options.summary: A JSON lines file on its own branch, one commit per train.

options.label: One commit per train on main
options.summary: docs/delivery/log.jsonl appended once per train; adds a commit to main each time.

decisions.question: Point 4: what does the pre-push hook do when it cannot reach GitHub?

options.label: Allow and warn
options.summary: The push goes through with a warning; the ready PR’s CI still decides the merge.

options.label: Refuse
options.summary: No push to a train branch until GitHub confirms CI finished; offline work stops.

decisions.question: Point 5: no online runner for a job’s labels before the ready PR opens?

options.label: Warn, don’t block
options.summary: join.py and ci_watch.py print a clear warning; works without admin rights.

options.label: Block the ready PR
options.summary: Refuse to open it until a runner is online; needs admin rights, else a warning.

decisions.question: Point 3: which tests run at the join when branches affect overlapping packages?

options.label: Union plus dependents
options.summary: Every package any branch affected plus their dependents, so an interaction is caught before the ready PR.

options.label: Union only
options.summary: Only the packages the branches affected; an interaction shows first in the ready PR’s CI.
